Numbers in this video are rough estimates to build intuition, not exact figures.

In reality, training cost depends on many factors like dataset size and quality, number of tokens, model architecture, hardware setup (type and number of GPUs), system efficiency, parallelization strategy, and how many times you retrain or tune the model.

Also, training doesn’t happen on a single GPU. Large models are trained on hundreds or even thousands of GPUs in parallel. So instead of one GPU running for 30,000 hours, it’s many GPUs running together for a much shorter time.

GPU pricing also varies a lot depending on provider, availability, and scale. The $3/hour number is not universal.

Another important point: model performance is not just about the number of parameters. Data quality, architecture design, and training techniques matter just as much, if not more.

Even reported numbers like GPT-4’s parameter count are not officially confirmed, so take such figures as approximations.

So don’t take the exact numbers literally. Focus on the bigger idea: building large AI models requires massive compute, high-quality data, and multiple iterations.
